item.title: Moldova: unauthenticated e-government services queried for about one million ID numbers; data on 750,000 extracted
item.description: Moldova's Electronic Governance Agency says that between 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-23 attackers exploited flaws in state digital services reachable without authentication to query about one million national identification numbers and, on preliminary estimates, extract data sets for about 750,000 of them, then used what they obtained to extract more from interconnected systems. The Prime Minister says foreign state involvement is being investigated and that AI allegedly helped find the flaws; Moldova has not attributed the attack, and the agency took 82 services under review and disconnected exposed services and more than 30 systems.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLENATOA2

Moldova's government digital services: attackers used flaws in services reachable without authentication to query about one million national identification numbers and extract data on about 750,000 of them between 19 and 23 October, and the Prime Minister says AI allegedly helped find the flaws

Moldova's Electronic Governance Agency (AGE) reported on 2026-10-27 that between 19 and 23 October attackers queried about one million national identification numbers (IDNPs) through state digital services and that, on preliminary estimates, data sets for about 750,000 of them were extracted; MOLDPRES had put the access requests at about 11 million on 2026-10-24 (Moldova Electronic Governance Agency, 2026-10-27; MOLDPRES, 2026-10-24). AGE's technical explanation is that the attackers exploited vulnerabilities in services reachable without authentication and then used the data they obtained for further extractions; the first attacks hit an electronic service that logged the legal basis of processing incorrectly, which is why citizens saw entries for civil-status document requests and driving-licence issue in the data-access history of the EVO app (Moldova Electronic Governance Agency, 2026-10-27). Data that may be affected, not every category for every person, includes name, date and place of birth, first-degree relatives, insured status, family doctor, social benefits, pensions, disability, driving licence, photograph, vehicles and companies owned or run, IBAN, tax debts and payment history; AGE says card data is not held on the platform and it found no unauthorised change to state registers (Moldova Electronic Governance Agency, 2026-10-27).

AGE stopped the extraction on 23 October at 11:30, reviewed 82 digital services and suspended the exposed ones, and its timeline says 82 public services and more than 30 information systems and administration panels were disconnected as a precaution on 23 October; it blocked further attempts on 25 and 27 October, and the Prime Minister's account is that 30 of the 82 services were disconnected (Moldova Electronic Governance Agency, 2026-10-27; MOLDPRES, 2026-10-28). The Prime Minister says the incident is not isolated, that foreign state actors are being investigated and that the attackers automated the extraction, with the use of artificial intelligence allegedly facilitating the identification and exploitation of the vulnerabilities (MOLDPRES, 2026-10-28). Moldova has not attributed the attack to any country or group (The Record, 2026-10-28).

Exposure
A public e-service of a federal, cantonal or communal administration that returns person data for an identifier without authentication, or whose output feeds other registers, since AGE says the extraction chained from unauthenticated services into further data (Moldova Electronic Governance Agency, 2026-10-27).
Detection
Citizens noticed the abuse because the data-access history in the EVO app showed processing for civil-status document requests and driving-licence issue that they had not made, so a data-subject-visible access log is a detection channel (Moldova Electronic Governance Agency, 2026-10-27). On the server side the relevant telemetry is per-service request volume and sequential or bulk identifier lookups from one source; the sources give no breakdown of the request pattern, so that is an inference from about 11 million requests against about one million numbers.
Defender takeaway
List the public services that answer for a person identifier without authentication and check what each one returns, whether it feeds other registers and whether its access log records the true purpose; rate limits and alerts on bulk lookups belong in front of every such service.

item.title: WatchGuard fixes three feature-dependent unauthenticated flaws scored 9.2 in Fireware OS; no exploitation known
item.description: WatchGuard's advisories of 2026-10-27 fix 17 flaws in Fireware OS 2026.4, 12.12.4 and, for T15 and T35 models, 12.5.22, seven of them scored 9.0 or higher. Three need no authentication but a specific feature: a heap write in the Access Portal's WebSocket handling, a stack overflow in the SIP proxy and missing authentication in the FireCluster sync daemon, each scored 9.2. Four more need an attacker who controls or intercepts traffic to an Active Directory server, to WatchGuard Cloud or to a log server. WatchGuard is not aware of exploitation of any of them.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLECVE-2026-93866 +6NATOA2

WatchGuard Fireware OS 2026.4, 12.12.4 and 12.5.22: seven of 17 fixed Fireware OS flaws are scored 9.0 or higher, among them unauthenticated memory-corruption and missing-authentication rows in the Access Portal, the SIP proxy and the FireCluster sync daemon; WatchGuard knows of no exploitation

WatchGuard's advisory listing of 2026-10-27 opens with 18 rows, 17 for Fireware OS and one for Mobile VPN with SSL Client for Windows, and seven of the 17 are scored 9.0 or higher (WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27). The fixes are in Fireware OS 2026.4, 12.12.4 and, for T15 and T35 models, 12.5.22. Three of the seven need no authentication but a specific feature. CVE-2026-93866 (9.2) is an integer overflow in the WebSocket handling of the Access Portal that lets a remote unauthenticated attacker write beyond the bounds of a heap buffer while the Access Portal is enabled (WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27). CVE-2026-93857 (9.2) is a stack buffer overflow in the SIP proxy that gives remote code execution when a SIP proxy is configured on the Firebox (WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27). CVE-2026-93865 (9.2) is missing authentication in the FireCluster synchronization daemon: a remote unauthenticated attacker invokes privileged administrative actions with a crafted request to the FireCluster management IP when clustering is enabled (WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27).

The other four need a network position. CVE-2026-112709 and CVE-2026-112710 (9.2 each) are heap overflows in the authentication service that give denial of service and possibly code execution to an attacker who controls or intercepts traffic to the configured Active Directory server and returns a crafted response (WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27; WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27). CVE-2026-103594 (9.5) is a stack overflow in WireGuard configuration processing for a man-in-the-middle with TLS-decrypted access between a Firebox that acts as a FireCloud Gateway and WatchGuard Cloud (WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27). CVE-2026-103593 (9.1) is a stack overflow in the logging service that gives root code execution to a network-adjacent attacker who impersonates or intercepts traffic to the log server with a crafted certificate, in FIPS mode (WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27). Six rows affect Fireware OS 2025.1 up to before 2026.4 and 12.0 up to before 12.12.4, T15 and T35 up to before 12.5.22, the WireGuard row starts at 2026.2 and 12.12, and each page states that WatchGuard is not aware of exploitation in the wild (WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27; WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27; WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27; WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27; WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27; WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27; WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27).

Exposure
A Firebox on a Fireware OS release inside those ranges with at least one of the listed features: the Access Portal, a SIP proxy policy, FireCluster membership, an Active Directory authentication server, the FireCloud Gateway role, or FIPS mode with an external log server; the three unauthenticated rows are reachable by any host that can reach the Access Portal, the SIP proxy policy or the cluster management address (WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27; WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27; WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27; WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27; WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27; WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27; WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27).
Detection
WatchGuard publishes no indicator and no workaround. For the three unauthenticated rows, connections to the cluster management address from hosts that are not cluster peers, WebSocket upgrade requests to the Access Portal from unexpected sources, SIP traffic from outside expected carriers, and restarts of the portal, SIP or sync services on the Firebox are the telemetry to review; this is an inference from the stated mechanisms.
Defender takeaway
Install the fixed release on appliances with the Access Portal, a SIP proxy or clustering first; where an upgrade has to wait, turn off a feature that is not used and keep the cluster management address off untrusted segments.

item.title: Veeam fixes an unauthenticated 9.1 authorization bypass on 13.x servers, a VB365 SQL injection and a ONE MFA bypass
item.description: Veeam's advisories of 2026-10-27 fix CVE-2026-108142, an unauthenticated authorization bypass on the CDP Coordinator Service of Veeam Backup & Replication 13.1 and 13.0 on Windows and of the Veeam Software Appliance (CVSS 4.0 9.1, fixed in 13.1.2 and 13.0.3; 12.x is not affected), a SQL injection in Veeam Backup for Microsoft 365 that reaches code execution as the PostgreSQL service account (9.0, fixed in 8.6) and an MFA bypass in Veeam ONE 13.1 for an attacker holding Administrator credentials (8.5). NCSC Switzerland relayed the Backup & Replication and Veeam ONE advisories on 2026-10-28; Veeam reports no exploitation.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLECVE-2026-108142 +5NATOA2

CVE-2026-108142, Veeam Backup & Replication: an unauthenticated authorization bypass on the CDP Coordinator Service of 13.x backup servers (CVSS 4.0 9.1), fixed in 13.1.2 and 13.0.3, with a Backup for Microsoft 365 SQL injection to code execution and a Veeam ONE MFA bypass fixed the same day

Veeam published three advisories on 2026-10-27. In Backup & Replication, CVE-2026-108142 (CVSS 4.0 9.1, critical) lets an unauthenticated attacker bypass authorization on the CDP Coordinator Service of Windows-based Backup & Replication and of the Veeam Software Appliance; it affects 13.1.1.18 and all earlier 13.1 builds and 13.0.2.29 and all earlier 13.0 builds, is fixed in 13.1.2 (build 13.1.2.57) and 13.0.3 (build 13.0.3.63), and does not affect 12.x (Veeam KB4948, 2026-10-27). The same advisory fixes two medium path-traversal flaws that need the Restore Operator role plus control over the contents of a backed-up NAS share and that write attacker-controlled files to an arbitrary path on the backup server, and a local privilege escalation in Veeam Agent for Linux version 13.1.1.4 and earlier that applies only to agents managed by a Backup & Replication server (Veeam KB4948, 2026-10-27). Veeam Backup for Microsoft 365 8.5.0.1014 and earlier carry CVE-2026-106076 (9.0, critical): an authenticated organization-transfer peer injects SQL into the source server's configuration database, which gives cross-tenant read and write of configuration data and remote code execution as the PostgreSQL service account; the fix is 8.6 (build 8.6.0.1102), as it is for CVE-2026-106077 (8.3), which lets a user with the Backup for Microsoft 365 Administrator role read arbitrary files on the backup server as LocalSystem; two further flaws, an unauthenticated REST API authentication bypass with a forged federation token (6.9) and an installer file-write (4.3), need 8.6 Patch 1 (build 8.6.0.5011) (Veeam KB4957, 2026-10-27). Veeam ONE 13.1.0.7233 and earlier let an attacker with valid Administrator credentials disable multi-factor authentication globally before completing MFA verification (8.5, high; fixed in 13.1 P1, build 13.1.0.7940) (Veeam KB4951, 2026-10-27).

NCSC Switzerland relayed the Backup & Replication and Veeam ONE advisories on 2026-10-28, lists the exploitation status as unknown with the vendor reporting no evidence of active exploitation, and gives the prerequisite for the critical flaw as network access to the backup server's CDP Coordinator Service (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-10-28). heise adds that backup servers are a favourite target of ransomware groups (translated from German) (heise online, 2026-10-28), and Veeam itself says attackers will likely try to reverse-engineer a disclosed patch to exploit unpatched deployments (Veeam KB4948, 2026-10-27).

Exposure
A Veeam Backup & Replication or Veeam Software Appliance on a 13.x build below 13.1.2 or 13.0.3 whose CDP Coordinator Service accepts connections from a network the attacker can reach; 12.x is out of scope (Veeam KB4948, 2026-10-27). Veeam Backup for Microsoft 365 version 8 below 8.6 Patch 1 (Veeam KB4957, 2026-10-27) and Veeam ONE 13.1 below Patch 1 (Veeam KB4951, 2026-10-27) are the other affected builds.
Detection
Veeam publishes no indicator. The telemetry that bears on this flaw is authentication and authorization events and service-account activity on the backup server, and new or changed backup jobs, repositories, stored credentials and restore operators; this is an inference from the described flaw, not a Veeam statement. For Veeam ONE, an MFA setting switched off followed by an Administrator sign-in is the sequence the flaw describes.
Defender takeaway
Install the fixed builds on every backup server first, since backup infrastructure is what ransomware groups try to reach before encrypting, and keep backup servers off networks that untrusted hosts can reach; where a backup server was reachable and unpatched, review its jobs, repositories and credentials for changes nobody made.

item.title: Talos: UAT-11473 implants KeyDrift in Cisco SD-WAN controllers through CVE-2026-20127 to collect data-plane keys
item.description: Cisco Talos reports that a cluster it calls UAT-11473 exploited CVE-2026-20127, the peering authentication bypass in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller, Manager and Validator (CVSS 10.0, fixed releases since February 2026, no workaround), and then ran the KeyDrift implant inside the controller's control-plane process to collect session metadata and what Talos assesses to be data-plane IPsec keys. Cisco's advisory, revised on 2026-10-28 to link Talos's post, says it is aware of limited exploitation, and Talos assesses with high confidence that the operating infrastructure overlaps considerably with Volt Typhoon's Silent Train network.
item.content:encoded:
HIGHCVE-2026-20127exploitedNATOB2

KeyDrift: Talos reports UAT-11473 exploiting CVE-2026-20127 in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN controllers to run an implant inside the control-plane daemon that collects data-plane keys, with infrastructure overlapping Volt Typhoon's Silent Train network

Cisco Talos reports that UAT-11473 exploited CVE-2026-20127, an authentication bypass in the peering authentication of Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-28), and then installed a custom framework it calls KeyDrift (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-28). CISA has listed the flaw in its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog since 2026-02-25 (CISA KEV, 2026-10-28). Cisco's advisory (CVSS 10.0) says an unauthenticated remote attacker can log in as an internal high-privileged non-root user and reach NETCONF to change the SD-WAN fabric configuration, and that there is no workaround (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-28). Cisco's advisory, revised on 2026-10-28 to link Talos's post, says its PSIRT is aware of limited exploitation (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-28). Lumen's Black Lotus Labs reported on 2026-10-28 that Volt Typhoon had exploited the flaw since late 2025 and after Cisco's February disclosure (Lumen Black Lotus Labs, 2026-10-28), and Talos assesses with high confidence that UAT-11473's operating infrastructure overlaps considerably with Volt Typhoon's Silent Train network (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-28).

KeyDrift runs inside the control-plane daemon. The actor edits the runit launchers of sshd and of a look-alike aaamgr service and remounts /rootfs.rw executable: the sshd launcher starts a script that injects the PolyFlame library into every running vdaemon process by ptrace, and the aaamgr launcher runs a packed PolyFlame loader directly (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-28). PolyFlame is tasked in-band over the control-plane traffic and offers a command, file-write and file-read backdoor and an intermediate command relay; Talos recovered no hardcoded address, port or domain (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-28). A second component, LittleFilch, hooks SSL_read in vdaemon and collects peer system addresses and 32-byte values Talos assesses to be OMP-distributed IPsec data-plane keys, writing them RSA-encrypted to /var/tmp (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-28). Talos lists observed targeting as space and satellite services, defense and aerospace technology, and policy research, calls the activity historical and does not say how many controllers were affected (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-28).

Exposure
Every Catalyst SD-WAN Controller, Manager and Validator regardless of configuration, on-premises or in Cisco's hosted clouds, on a release below the first fixed one in the advisory's table; Cisco says controllers with ports exposed to the internet are at risk (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-28).
Detection
On the controller's authentication log, Cisco says to audit /var/log/auth.log for accepted public-key logins of the vmanage-admin account from addresses that are not among the configured System IPs, and to validate control-connection peering events, those of peer type vmanage first, against maintenance windows and asset inventory (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-28). item.title: DeadTag: expired tag domains send visitors to iPhone exploit kits; opening the page is enough on vulnerable iOS
item.description: Report URI and iVerify report that an operator they call DeadTag buys the expired domains of old analytics and advertising tags that thousands of websites still load, so every page that carries the tag runs the operator's script, and sells the visitors on; Report URI counts more than 660 re-registered domains. For chosen iPhone visitors one chain ends at a page that serves the Coruna kit to iOS 13 to 17.2.1 and a modified DarkSword kit to iOS 18.4 to 18.7, both of which attack the browser itself, so that opening the page compromises a vulnerable device and steals keychain passwords and crypto-wallet data.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLENATOB2

DeadTag: re-registered domains of defunct analytics and advertising tags redirect visitors of thousands of sites, among them to a page that serves the Coruna and DarkSword iPhone exploit kits, which compromise a vulnerable device when the page opens

Report URI and iVerify describe a campaign they name DeadTag: attackers buy the expired domains behind old analytics and advertising tags that thousands of websites still load, so every page that still carries the tag runs the operator's script without the site owner changing or noticing anything, and the operator sells the visitors those tags bring in (Report URI, 2026-10-22). Report URI has identified more than 660 re-registered domains still embedded on thousands of sites and cautiously estimates 135 million visits a month (Report URI, 2026-10-22). The script is about 2 KB, does nothing for search engines, scanners and other bots, asks the operator's server what to do with each visitor and redirects the chosen ones, and Report URI found that the operator stopped answering when it probed from data-centre addresses or returned too often from residential ones; destinations include scam pages, a fake VPN pop-up and, for iPhones, a page that serves two exploit kits (Report URI, 2026-10-22).

One chain ends at a fake prediction-market page that picks the kit by the visitor's iOS version, Coruna for iOS 13 to 17.2.1 and a modified "P7" variant of DarkSword for iOS 18.4 to 18.7; both attack the browser itself, so opening the page is enough to compromise a vulnerable device, and the spyware they install steals keychain passwords, crypto-wallet app data and device and account information and reports to one server; Report URI notes that Coruna and DarkSword are separate exploit kits that have been seen in different campaigns, and that here both send their stolen data to the same server, which it reads as one operator running both (Report URI, 2026-10-22). iVerify reads DeadTag as mostly focused on European domains rather than .com (iVerify, 2026-10-21), and saw the P7 variant reach an employee's device at a customer organisation through a malicious Instagram ad while the employee was scrolling in the app (iVerify, 2026-10-21). The kit operator does not rely on DeadTag alone: Report URI found DarkSword loaders on hundreds of online shops on one e-commerce platform, PrestaShop (Report URI, 2026-10-22).

Exposure
Any public website that still loads a script from a third-party domain whose provider no longer operates it, where the browser fetches nothing useful and the page looks normal, and any iPhone on iOS 13 to 17.2.1 or 18.4 to 18.7 that opens such a page (Report URI, 2026-10-22).
Detection
Inventory the external script references of each public site and flag any whose domain has been re-registered or no longer belongs to its provider; Report URI recommends script monitoring that shows when a new script or domain appears on a page, and a Content Security Policy that controls which domains a site may load code from (Report URI, 2026-10-22). A security scanner usually sees only an empty response from the malicious script, because the operator answers only selected visitors.
Defender takeaway
Remove dead third-party tags from every site you run, enforce a Content Security Policy and keep iPhones on the current iOS, with Lockdown Mode for people who may be targeted; for an iPhone that may have opened an affected page, Report URI advises restarting it, changing the passwords stored in its keychain and moving crypto assets to a new wallet (Report URI, 2026-10-22).

item.title: PolyShell (CVE-2026-48356): Magento upload flaw attacked since March, fixed in July, CISA lists it as exploited
item.description: Sansec reports that PolyShell, the unauthenticated file upload in the Magento and Adobe Commerce REST API that Adobe tracks as CVE-2026-48356, has been attacked since 2026-03-19, with a mass wave on 2026-03-30 that put a JavaScript loader on 471 stores in one hour. Adobe's bulletin APSB26-73 of 2026-07-14 names the 2026-jul builds as the fix and still says Adobe knows of no exploits, while Sansec says Magento 2.4.9 carried a fix on 2026-05-12; CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-27. A store that ran an unpatched build may carry a webshell that the update does not remove.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLECVE-2026-48356exploitedNATOB2

CVE-2026-48356 (PolyShell), Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source: an unauthenticated file upload attacked since March 2026, fixed for supported lines in July, and listed by CISA as exploited on 2026-10-27

Sansec named the flaw PolyShell: a missing validation in Magento's REST API that lets unauthenticated attackers upload executable files to a store, using a polyglot (code disguised as an image) to pass the image check (Sansec, 2026-03-17). It reports that its Shield service has blocked exploitation attempts against 79.5% of the Magento stores it protects since 2026-03-16, with first attacks observed on 2026-03-19, and that the vulnerable code has existed since the first Magento 2 release (Sansec, 2026-03-17). On 2026-03-30 a mass wave uploaded webshells, spread backdoor scripts across several directories and injected a JavaScript loader into the CMS pages of 471 stores within one hour (Sansec, 2026-03-30).

Sansec dates a fix in Magento 2.4.9 to 2026-05-12, without a backport to the supported 2.4.8 and 2.4.7 lines, and the backport to those lines to 2026-07-14, in bulletin APSB26-73 (Sansec, 2026-03-17). That bulletin rates the flaw Critical at CVSS 3.1 9.6, lists 2.4.9 among the affected versions, names the 2026-jul builds, 2.4.9-2026-jul included, as the fix for Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source, and still says Adobe is not aware of any exploits in the wild (Adobe, 2026-07-14). CISA added CVE-2026-48356 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-27 on evidence of active exploitation and gives no detail (CISA, 2026-10-27; CISA KEV, 2026-10-27). Sansec's research of 2026-10-24 shows the operator behind the March wave still active: its newest loader domain, registered on 2026-10-06, sits in the CMS blocks of 83 stores, 60 of which already carried an earlier loader, and one of them, on Magento 2.4.7-p1, still lacks APSB26-73 and holds PolyShell webshells disguised as images (Sansec, 2026-10-24).

Exposure
Every Magento Open Source and Adobe Commerce store without the 2026-jul fix, 2.4.9 included (Adobe, 2026-07-14); the anonymous guest-cart item routes need no credentials, and the upload becomes code execution on stock nginx for the oldest 2.x lines, on any non-stock nginx that hands every .php file to the PHP handler, and on Magento before 2.3.5 running on Apache without the engine switch set for that directory (Sansec, 2026-03-17).
Detection
Sansec calls any .php, .phtml or .phar file in the custom-options upload directory a strong indicator of compromise, and the uploaded file stays on disk even where execution is blocked (Sansec, 2026-03-17); also look for requests that add items to guest carts with embedded file data from unfamiliar sources (Sansec, 2026-03-17), script tags in the CMS block table and administrator accounts nobody created (Sansec, 2026-10-24).
Defender takeaway
Install the fix now, and treat a store that ran an unpatched build while internet-reachable since March as possibly compromised until its upload directory, CMS blocks and administrator accounts are checked, because an uploaded file stays on disk even where execution is blocked (Sansec, 2026-03-17), so the fix does not remove a shell already written (an inference), and deleting a loader script does not remove the access behind it (Sansec, 2026-10-24).

item.title: Inside IT: SafePay published about 49 GB from a Bernese wastewater association; the association declines to comment
item.description: SafePay claimed an attack on the Bernese wastewater-treatment association ARA-Region Lyss-Limpachtal on 2026-09-15, and Inside IT reports of 2026-10-27 that the group has now put about 49 GB of stolen data into the darknet. Risikomonitor's analysis, which Inside IT relays and which is not verified independently, finds data on more than 1,200 identifiable persons, bank statements, 255 password hits in files and a third party's monitoring-portal credentials stored on the association's server; the association will not comment, and no source says how the attackers got in.
item.content:encoded:
ROUTINENATOC3

ARA-Region Lyss-Limpachtal (canton Bern, communal wastewater-treatment association): SafePay has put about 49 GB into the darknet, which Risikomonitor's analysis, relayed by Inside IT, finds holds personal records, bank statements, weak passwords and a third party's monitoring credentials; the association declines to comment

The tracker DeXpose recorded on 2026-09-15 that SafePay had claimed an attack on ARA Lyss, the wastewater-treatment association at ara-lyss.ch, posting that the full leak would be published soon unless a company representative made contact (DeXpose, 2026-09-15). Inside IT reported on 2026-10-27 that SafePay has put the stolen data into the darknet, about 49 GB in the case of the Bernese association ARA-Region Lyss-Limpachtal, that the security firm Risikomonitor analysed it, and that the association's management declined to comment (Inside IT, 2026-10-27). Risikomonitor's analysis, relayed by Inside IT and not verified independently, finds about 3,200 e-mail addresses and data on more than 1,200 identifiable persons; user folders and a data store with content up to March 2026 that hold 255 password hits, 195 of them very weak; bank statements and a transaction list with more than 100 payments by private persons with name and address; the full login data to the monitoring portals of the photovoltaic plants of another company's customers, stored on the same server; and a 2015 applicant list with birth dates, civil status, former employer and interview notes that was never deleted (Inside IT, 2026-10-27).

BACS told Inside IT that SafePay, which relies on double extortion, is among the more active ransomware groups in Switzerland and, together with The Gentlemen, the third most active in 2026 after Akira and Payload, that it has no clear focus on Switzerland, and that it was first observed there in May 2025 (Inside IT, 2026-10-27). No source says how the attackers got in or that data was encrypted at the association.

Defender takeaway
A communal body or association should look for credentials, bank statements and applicant files on its own file servers before an attacker does: Risikomonitor found 255 password hits in files, another company's portal logins and a 2015 applicant list that had never been deleted, and those are what a published dump gives fraudsters (Inside IT, 2026-10-27).

item.title: Update: The Joomla extension disclosure wave adds a cookie-forgery auth bypass, one anonymous request reaches Super User, and Super User means PHP
item.description: Balbooa released Gridbox 2.20.4.2 on 2026-10-27, fixing two unauthenticated read-side SQL injections, CVE-2026-102788 (the sort-by parameter of store and category post lists) and CVE-2026-102789 (an editor task without a permission check), both scored CVSS 4.0 9.3 by the Joomla CNA and affecting every release up to 2.20.4.1. No exploitation is reported, Joomla 3 sites have no fix, and the action now points at 2.20.4.2.
item.content:encoded:
Update28 Oct 2026 03:52 UTCrun 2026-10-28T0256Z-intelactionsbodycvesevidencesourcessourcing_notesummary

Balbooa released Gridbox 2.20.4.2 on 2026-10-27, fixing two unauthenticated read-side SQL injections, CVE-2026-102788 (the sort-by parameter of store and category post lists) and CVE-2026-102789 (an editor task without a permission check), both scored CVSS 4.0 9.3 by the Joomla CNA and affecting every release up to 2.20.4.1. No exploitation is reported, Joomla 3 sites have no fix, and the action now points at 2.20.4.2.

Balbooa released Gridbox 2.20.4.2 on 2026-10-27 with two security fixes rated Critical, for the versions 2.20.4.1 and earlier (Balbooa, 2026-10-27). CVE-2026-102788 is in the sort-by URL parameter of store and category post lists and CVE-2026-102789 is a missing permission check on the editor task that loads blog posts (mySites.guru, 2026-10-27); Balbooa's fixes are a strict allowlist validation for the sort-by parameter and a user edit-level check on the editor task (Balbooa, 2026-10-27). mySites.guru says the sort value previously went into the ORDER BY part of the database query and reads the second flaw as a second anonymous route to the same query. mySites.guru reports that the Joomla CNA scores both CVSS 4.0 9.3 and lists every release from 1.0.0 to 2.20.4.1 as affected, and that only two PHP files differ between 2.20.4.1 and 2.20.4.2, one per fix (mySites.guru, 2026-10-27).

Both flaws read data: an anonymous visitor can extract the Joomla user table, with its password hashes, and every other table the site's extensions created. mySites.guru says about 95% of the Gridbox sites it monitors ran an affected version on the morning of the release, that sites on the Joomla 3 line stop at Gridbox 2.17.0.2, which has no fix for this year's flaws, and that there is no public report of exploitation yet (mySites.guru, 2026-10-27). Nothing here is reported exploited, unlike the July batches above; the version to be on is now 2.20.4.2.

Detection
In web access and database query logs, store or category list requests whose sort-by value is not one of the known sort keys, repeated anonymous calls to the Gridbox editor's blog-post task, and slow-query bursts from the web account; because the flaws only read, the post-patch check is credential hygiene on a site that was exposed, starting with administrator accounts nobody created, since the password hashes can be worked on offline.
Defender takeaway
Update to 2.20.4.2 now, communal and agency sites included, and move Joomla 3 sites to a supported Joomla (mySites.guru, 2026-10-27).

item.title: HPE ClearPass 6.14, 6.12 and 6.11 are affected by PHP2Shell; a hotfix patch exists for each train

NOTABLECVE-2026-109618 +1exploitedupdatedNATOA2

CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, HPE Networking ClearPass Policy Manager: bulletin HPESBNW05171 lists the 6.14, 6.12 and 6.11 trains as affected by the PHP2Shell flaws and names a hotfix patch for each (CVSS 3.1 9.8)

HPE Networking's bulletin HPESBNW05171, released on 2026-10-22 and revised on 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-29, covers CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, the PHP flaws behind PHP2Shell, in ClearPass Policy Manager and scores each CVSS 3.1 9.8 with network access, no privileges and no user interaction (HPE Networking, 2026-10-29). Its affected-products note lists ClearPass 6.14.0 and earlier in the 6.14 release train and 6.11.15 and earlier in the 6.11 train, while its machine-readable record also lists the 6.12 train and gives 6.14.1, 6.11.16 and 6.12.8 as the boundaries; the bulletin does not reconcile the two (HPE Networking, 2026-10-29). The fix is a hotfix patch for each train, 6.14.1, 6.12.8 (added in revision 3, which HPE says "exceptionally" includes 6.12.8) and 6.11.16, downloadable from the HPE Networking Support Portal; versions past end of maintenance are presumed affected and are not covered, and HPE has not assessed versions past end of support, which it says should be considered potentially impacted (HPE Networking, 2026-10-29).

HPE recommends confining the CLI and web management interfaces to a dedicated layer 2 segment or VLAN, or controlling them with firewall policy at layer 3 and above, and asks customers to consider removing guest portals and all management interfaces from public access until the affected ClearPass instances have been upgraded (HPE Networking, 2026-10-29). Other HPE Networking products and software versions it does not list are not known to be affected, and for Mist products the bulletin points to a Juniper reference advisory (HPE Networking, 2026-10-29). CISA added both PHP flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26 (CISA KEV, 2026-10-27); the bulletin itself says nothing about exploitation of ClearPass (HPE Networking, 2026-10-29).

Exposure
Every ClearPass Policy Manager on the 6.14, 6.12 or 6.11 train without the hotfix patch; the guest portal and the management interfaces are the surfaces HPE asks to take off public access (HPE Networking, 2026-10-29).
Detection
HPE gives no indicator and no post-patch check; CISA's PHP alert advises monitoring for PHP worker processes launching shells or downloading tools (CISA, 2026-10-21), which on a ClearPass node would be processes started by the web worker account (an inference, since HPE does not describe how ClearPass runs PHP).
Defender takeaway
Install the hotfix patch for 6.14.1, 6.12.8 or 6.11.16 on every node now, the remediation HPE's bulletin names, and take any guest portal or management interface reachable from untrusted networks off public access, as HPE asks (HPE Networking, 2026-10-29).

item.description: IDC Frontier's seventh report of 2026-10-27, which closes the investigation, names the cause: an open-source flaw in the authentication system of its customer portal, after which the attacker took administrator rights on the virtualisation platform through the management console and encrypted the virtual servers; it replaces the entry's statement that the intrusion route is not public.

Update28 Oct 2026 03:44 UTCrun 2026-10-28T0256Z-inteltitleheadlinesummarytechniquessourcesevidencesourcing_notebodyclassificationverification

IDC Frontier's seventh report of 2026-10-27, which closes the investigation, names the cause: an open-source flaw in the authentication system of its customer portal, after which the attacker took administrator rights on the virtualisation platform through the management console and encrypted the virtual servers; it replaces the entry's statement that the intrusion route is not public.

IDC Frontier's seventh report of 2026-10-27 says its investigation with an external security firm is complete and names the cause: a third party exploited a vulnerability in open-source software used in the authentication system of the IDCF Cloud Portal, the portal customers use to start virtual servers and check billing, and so entered that system (translated from Japanese; IDC Frontier, 2026-10-27). The attacker then obtained administrator rights on the virtualisation platform through the management console, stopped customers' virtual servers and encrypted them; the software is not named. The provider finds no trace of customer data leaving the virtual servers, says the improper queries of portal registration data reached up to 71 customers, up from 48, that up to four customer login passwords were improperly changed and have been reset, and that backups are retrievable for 206 customers. It is rebuilding the portal in a new environment, replacing the affected authentication system with an external identity provider and limiting portal access to customer IP addresses with mandatory multi-factor authentication.

Update28 Oct 2026 03:43 UTCrun 2026-10-28T0256Z-intelheadlinesummarysourcesevidencesourcing_notebody

A second Swiss customer of Camping.Care, Campingplatz Hüttenberg in canton Thurgau, has warned its guests of the same WhatsApp fraud in a notice with the page date 2026-10-23; the notice says the supplier is investigating the cause and does not mention PHP, so the link to the PHP flaws rests on SRF, Blick and a TCS spokesperson's statement rather than on the supplier.

Netzwoche reported on 2026-10-27 that a second Swiss Camping.Care customer, Campingplatz Hüttenberg in canton Thurgau, has warned its guests of WhatsApp messages about existing bookings that contain real booking information and a link; the campsite's notice carries the page date 2026-10-23 (Netzwoche, 2026-10-27; Campingplatz Hüttenberg, 2026-10-23). The notice says Camping.care informed the campsite of the messages, that Camping.care is investigating the cause and that booking data must be assumed to have been used without authorisation; it does not mention PHP, and Netzwoche points out that it does not say whether the attackers used one of the PHP flaws. The link to the PHP flaws therefore rests on SRF, Blick and a TCS spokesperson's statement to Keystone-SDA (watson.ch, 2026-10-26), not on the supplier.
